Methods for simple_mvc objects

Source: R/methods.simple_mconv.R, R/methods.simple_mvc.R
simple_mvc-methods.Rd

Methods defined for objects returned from method_vc().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
predict(object, newdata, from = NULL, to = NULL, level = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
print(x, digits = 4, scale = c("analysis", "original"), at = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.simple_mvc'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
confint(object, parm = c("all", "bias", "sd"), level = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("ba", "matrix", "vc"),
  pair = NULL,
  pair_seed = NULL,
  geom = c("geom_point", "geom_bin2d", "geom_density_2d", "geom_density_2d_filled",
    "stat_density_2d"),
  delta = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'simple_mvc'
check(
  x,
  pair_seed = NULL,
  error.ratio = NULL,
  bias_line = c("adjusted", "expected"),
  ...
)

Arguments

newdata, from, to

Passed to the predict method of method_convert() results: values of the from method (original scale) to convert to the to method, with prediction limits.

level

For confint, the confidence level, by default the conf_level used in method_vc(); other levels are recomputed from the stored standard errors and degrees of freedom. For predict, the coverage of the prediction limits (default: the pred_level of the fit).

...

further arguments passed through, see description of return value for details.

x, object

Object of class simple_mvc, as returned from method_vc().

digits

The number of digits to print.

scale

For print, the scale of the bias, limits, and repeatability coefficients: "analysis" (default), the scale set by transform, or "original", back-transformed to the units of the measurements at the level(s) in at. Ignored without a transformation. See details.

at

For print with scale = "original", the level(s), in original units, at which to express the results. Default (NULL) is the median of the item averages (computed on the analysis scale and back-transformed). Supplying at implies scale = "original".

parm

Which parameters to include: "all" (default), "bias", or "sd" (variance component SDs).

type

Type of plot. "ba" (default): a Bland-Altman plot of the differences for one pair of methods, with the bias and limits drawn as points to the left of the data, as in agreement_limit(): the whiskers show the confidence interval of the bias and the confidence bounds of the limits of agreement (with interval = "tolerance", the points are the prediction limits and the whiskers extend to the tolerance limits). "matrix": all pairs, with the methods named on the diagonal, each pair of methods plotted against each other above it (identity line dashed; constant-bias conversion line with prediction limits on the original scale), and Bland-Altman plots below it. "vc": estimates and confidence intervals of the variance component SDs and the repeatability coefficients.

pair

Character vector naming the two methods to plot, in the order of the difference (first minus second). Default is the first pair.

pair_seed

Seed for the random pairing of exchangeable replicates in the plot or in check(). The global random number generator state is restored afterwards. With exchangeable replicates and no seed, the pairing changes from call to call, and so do the plotted differences and the check() p-values (when items have unequal numbers of replicates by the two methods); set pair_seed for reproducible results.

geom

For type = "ba", the geometry used to display the data points: "geom_point" (default), "geom_bin2d", "geom_density_2d", "geom_density_2d_filled", or "stat_density_2d", as in loa-methods.

delta

For type = "ba", the maximal allowable difference, drawn as dashed lines: one value (drawn at delta and -delta, or, for ratios with transform = "log", at delta and 1/delta) or two values, on the plotted scale.

error.ratio

For check, an optional known ratio of the measurement error variances of the two methods, var(error of the first) / var(error of the second), as in dem_reg(), on the analysis scale. Used only with two methods and one measurement per item.

bias_line

For check with replicates or error.ratio, the dashed line on the level dependence panel: "adjusted" (default; the error-adjusted slope) or "expected" (the slope expected from unequal measurement error alone). See "Choosing bias_line" in loa-methods for the pros and cons.

Value

print

Prints the biases, limits, and variance components. With transform = "log", biases and limits are shown as ratios; with scale = "original", in original units at the level(s) in at.

coef

Named vector: method means averaged over items (alpha_<method>) and the variance component SDs (tau, omega, sigma_<method>, on the transformed scale).

vcov

Covariance matrix of the method means.

summary

An object of class summary.simple_mvc whose print method shows the design (number of items by method and number of replicates), biases, variance components with confidence limits and df, limits, and repeatability coefficients.

confint

Matrix of confidence limits for the biases and the variance component SDs.

plot

A ggplot object (type = "ba" or "vc") or a patchwork object (type = "matrix").

check

A patchwork of diagnostic plots, as for agreement_limit(), with what to look for in each subtitle and the tests in the captions: normal QQ plots of the standardized residuals by method and of the predicted random effects (Shapiro-Wilk tests, or Kolmogorov-Smirnov with 5000 or more values); and, for each pair, the homogeneity of variance of the differences (square root of the absolute standardized differences against the averages, Breusch-Pagan test) and proportional bias (centred differences against the averages, with a regression line). The tests for each pair use item means, so replicates are not counted more than once. With replicates, the test of the slope is corrected for unequal measurement error (and, with tau = "method", unequal method-by-item variances), and the error-adjusted slope is drawn dashed; see "Proportional bias diagnostic" in loa-methods. A message suggests alternatives when the slope or the Breusch-Pagan test has p < 0.05. The proportional bias results are attached as the attribute "prop_bias", one row per pair (named in group); beta is the scale of the second method of the pair relative to the first.

Details

With a transformation, a constant bias and constant limits on the analysis scale correspond, in original units, to a bias and limits that depend on the level. print(x, scale = "original") expresses them at a given level \(t\) (on the analysis scale): a difference \(d\) between the methods, centered on that level, is \(h(d) = g^{-1}(t + d/2) - g^{-1}(t - d/2)\) in original units, where \(g^{-1}\) is the inverse transformation. For a fixed level, \(h\) is increasing in \(d\), so the limits, their confidence bounds, and the prediction and tolerance limits keep their coverage and confidence exactly, and the back-transformed bias is the median difference at that level (not the mean). The repeatability coefficients are converted in the same way. The SDs and variance components stay on the analysis scale. Differences are centered on the level of the two measurements, as on the x-axis of a Bland-Altman plot, unlike predict(), which starts from a measurement by one method.
